notes.decision: Fits with guardrails: keep saved recovery-point evidence visible, explain why database restoration is unavailable, and omit unusable confirmation and Restore controls. The approved restore refusal remains authoritative.
notes.persona: Operator deciding whether to install a release and understanding available recovery.
notes.navigationLayer: Existing contextual action; no route or navigation addition.
notes.reuse: Existing owner release card, risk notice and recovery/history presentation; shared pure recovery-eligibility owner serves server and live client.
notes.sourceTruth: Fresh SelfUpgradeRun recovery evidence plus the canonical restore-eligibility policy. A saved backup alone never grants restoration. No caller-supplied retention proof or permission flag.
notes.emptyAndFailure: Missing or incomplete recovery point, running run, retained historical rollback and unproven retention remain distinct. Database restoration is unavailable until review history can be preserved safely. Conditional prior-version fallback is not promised as universal recovery.
notes.aiBoundary: The page change sends no coworker prompt. Native advisory UX critique CE-7F4B1050 was requested separately under the UX-fit skill; it is not a delivered verdict.
notes.prototype: docs/ux-fit/2026-10-22-review-reassessment-restore-availability.html was authored before the implementation plan. Option A has zero unusable restore controls; Option B retains two disabled controls.
notes.verification: Final-source regression tests, both TypeScript programs, independent source review, exhaustive canonical gate and protected served route sweep are required. Actual results are recorded in Workroom WC-A5703D01 and PR6546; prototype exercise does not establish deployed acceptance.
